To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The state of reduction of NAD in liver is a key factor in the regulation of hep-atic protein synthesis.

1) the administration of octanoateto rats in vivo increased hepatic protein synthesis and decreased the phosphorylaiton potential; 2) the acute administration of ethanol increased the hepatic state of reduction and decreased the phosphorylaton potential, however, protein synthesis was unaffected; and 3) a rise in the hepatic state reduction of the NADS system is not effective at decreasing protein synthesis in vivo, unless it is accompanied with a decrease in the hepatic phosphorylation potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of changes in the state of oxidation and phosphorylation on hepatic protein synthesis.
the role of the NAD and ATP systems in the regulation of protein synthesis in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phosphorylation state of the adenylate system is the primary regulator of hepatic protein synthetic rates in the rat.
the state of reduction and phosphorylation potential of the NADH/NAD+ system are important in the regulation of protein synthesis.
a decrease in the NADH/NAD+ ratio is not effective in depressing hepatic protein synthesis unless it is accompanied with a decrease in the ATP concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the state of reduction and phosphorylation of the hepatic adenine nucleotide system are important regulators of protein synthesis and that these two factors are interdependent in vivo.

in the rat in the post-absorptive state, hepatic protein synthesis is regulated in vivo by a decrease in phosphorylation potential and that the effect is mediated by a rise in the concentration of the allosteric inhibitor of the initiation factor, eIF-2, P-eIF-2.
the state of reduction per se is not an effective regulator of hepatic protein metabolism, whereas changes in phosphorylation potential are.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the state of reduction is not a reliable indicator of a decrease in the rate of protein synthesis in vivo.
the NAD system can be manipulated by various agents and this manipulation has a profound effect on the regulation of protein synthesis in vivo.
